name: Thunkable
tagline: Prototype a mobile app with fixed components and local data

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 2,000 AI tokens/month; 3 public projects; 5 screens/project; 0 private projects; 0 live published apps
tiers.notes: Private projects and ongoing published-app availability require a paid plan.

tiers.name: Accelerator
tiers.limits: 20,000 AI tokens/month; 5 public projects; 1 private project; 10 screens/project; 0 live apps
tiers.notes: The official pricing DOM exposed $18 and $19 with conflicting billing labels; values are recorded conservatively as annual/monthly.

tiers.name: Builder
tiers.limits: 50,000 AI tokens/month; unlimited public projects; 10 private projects; unlimited screens; 1 live app

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 100,000 AI tokens/month; unlimited public/private projects and screens; multiple live-app and collaboration features

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom users, apps, governance, support and contract terms

tiers.name: Education
tiers.limits: Custom classroom, educator and institution terms

pricing.freeTierCaps: 2,000 AI tokens/month; 3 public projects; 5 screens/project; 0 private projects; 0 live apps
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; exact Accelerator labels were inconsistent in the official page markup
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI tokens reset and expire each month; additional token packs cost extra at unpublished rates, an active paid plan is needed to keep private/published apps available, and Apple/Google developer accounts are separate

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Thunkable, prototype a mobile app with fixed components and local data. The hard boundary is native build infrastructure, device integrations, publishing pipeline, and education ecosystem, plus connectors, runtime reliability, and governance.
coreLoopDIY: Prototype a mobile app from fixed components, define tables and views, build a constrained CRUD interface over local data or one approved data source, and deploy it for a small trusted team.
requirements: API credentials for one selected integration
whatYouLose: native build infrastructure, device integrations, publishing pipeline, and education ecosystem
ongoingBurden: schema migration, auth, permissions, connector drift, queues, deployments, backups, and auditability
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Thunkable because the builder is only useful when its runtime, connectors, permissions, and deployments remain boring for years. The recurring cost buys schema migration, auth, permissions, connector drift, queues, deployments, backups, and auditability, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Appsmith
priorArt.desc: Large open-source low-code platform for internal applications and data sources.

alternatives.name: MIT App Inventor
alternatives.desc: Blocks, fixed mobile components, local storage, and installable apps; aesthetically still very much MIT App Inventor.

facts.install: Use MIT's hosted web builder with the MIT AI2 Companion app, or build and operate the source on Google App Engine
facts.dataFormat: Projects created on MIT's public instance live in its hosted App Inventor service and can be exported as portable `.aia` ZIP archives containing screens, blocks, assets, and project metadata; compiled Android packages are downloaded separately. A self-hosted instance keeps the same project data in the operator's App Engine environment.
facts.gapVsPaid: MIT App Inventor covers block-based prototypes but offers much older-looking components, weaker responsive design, fewer production integrations, and less polished publishing than Thunkable.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted builder itself is clean, but live testing requires installing and pairing the Companion app; self-hosting is for experienced operators and needs a JDK, Ant, Google Cloud SDK, and a source build.

alternatives.name: Nowa Starter
alternatives.desc: A more modern visual mobile builder with local projects and source export; overkill for a prototype, but genuinely free.

facts.install: Hosted signup in the browser, or install Nowa Desktop for macOS/Windows and create a local Flutter project
facts.engines: Nowa's built-in AI agent uses plan-provided AI credits; its public product documentation does not identify the underlying model provider.
facts.dataFormat: Local projects are ordinary Flutter source-code folders on the user's machine; cloud projects live in Nowa's cloud, can be downloaded as full Flutter source, linked to GitHub, or cloned and synchronized to a local copy.
facts.gapVsPaid: Nowa produces real Flutter code, but that power adds a Flutter toolchain and developer concepts, making simple prototypes less immediate than Thunkable's fixed-component cloud builder.
facts.setupBlocker: Browser projects start cleanly; local development requires Nowa Desktop and a Flutter toolchain, with Xcode installed first on macOS, and the free plan does not include one-click native-store deployment.

alternatives.name: Thunkable Free
alternatives.desc: The same product is free for its stated job, prototyping with fixed components and local data, provided public projects are acceptable.

facts.install: Hosted signup; build in the browser and test with the Thunkable Live app or emailed Android test package
facts.engines: Thunkable's built-in generative-AI features consume plan AI tokens; the public pricing and documentation do not disclose the underlying models.
facts.dataFormat: Project screens, blocks, and assets live in Thunkable's cloud account; every free project is public and remixable in the Public Gallery. App runtime data can use on-device stored variables, Thunkable's default Firebase-backed cloud variables, or user-connected services.
facts.gapVsPaid: Thunkable Free is the same editor, but public projects, project and screen limits, and restricted private publishing make it unsuitable for work that cannot be exposed or kept tiny.
facts.setupBlocker: The free plan's first hard stop is privacy and scope: only three public projects, five screens per project, 100 MB total project storage, and no private project.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Builder plan and a small-team internal app DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Thunkable in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: prototype a mobile app from fixed components, define tables and views, build a constrained CRUD interface over local data or one approved data source, and deploy it for a small trusted team.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a schema editor for text, number, boolean, date, enum, and relation fields.
Generate list, detail, create, edit, and kanban views from the schema.
Implement role-based read and write rules for admin and member roles.
Support one REST connector with encrypted credentials and explicit field mapping.
Add an activity log, CSV import or export, backups, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with migrations and a seeded example workspace.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out arbitrary user-authored code execution.
Deliberately leave out a broad integration marketplace.
Deliberately leave out native mobile binaries and enterprise compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
